summary: The article provides a largely accurate overview of PRIM, PMS, and Mutual Funds, including their investment minimums, fees, and general taxation principles, based on recent SEBI regulations.

claims.claim: PRIM (Portfolio Managers' Route for Investing in Mutual Fund Units) is a new SEBI framework allowing PMS managers to build portfolios using mutual funds, ETFs, and SIFs, operating under the SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2026.
claims.note: SEBI approved the introduction of PRIM under the new SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2026, which replaces the 2020 regulations. PRIM allows portfolio managers to invest in direct plans of mutual funds, ETFs, index funds, and SIFs.

claims.claim: PRIM requires a minimum investment of ₹25 lakhs, while conventional PMS has a minimum of ₹50 lakhs.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm the minimum investment for PRIM is ₹25 lakhs and for conventional PMS is ₹50 lakhs.

claims.claim: The fixed management fee under PRIM is capped at a maximum of 1% of the client's AUM. Performance-based fees are also permitted.
claims.note: SEBI has capped the fixed management fee for PRIM at 1% of client AUM, and performance-linked fees are also allowed.

claims.claim: SEBI has capped investments in schemes of affiliated AMCs at 25% under PRIM to prevent potential conflicts of interest.
claims.note: Investments in schemes of affiliated, group, or associate AMCs under PRIM are capped at 25%.

claims.claim: For debt-oriented mutual funds acquired on or after April 1, 2023, gains are taxed as per the investor's income tax slab rate regardless of the holding period.
claims.note: Gains on debt mutual funds acquired on or after April 1, 2023, are taxed at slab rates regardless of the holding period.

claims.claim: For debt-oriented mutual funds acquired before April 1, 2023, gains are taxed as per the investor's income tax slab rate if held for up to 3 years (STCG), and at 20% with indexation benefit if held for more than 3 years (LTCG).
claims.note: For debt mutual funds acquired before April 1, 2023, gains are taxed at slab rates if held for up to 3 years (STCG), and at 20% with indexation benefit if held for more than 3 years (LTCG).

claims.claim: Short-term capital gains on listed equities (PMS) are taxed at 15%, while long-term capital gains on listed equities (over 1 year holding) exceeding ₹1 lakh are taxed at 10%.
claims.note: For PMS, STCG on listed equities is taxed at 20% (if held for 12 months or less), and LTCG on listed equities (over 12 months holding) exceeding ₹1.25 lakh is taxed at 12.5%. These rates are effective from July 23, 2024, and apply for FY 2025-26.

article_title: PRIM vs mutual funds vs PMS: Experts explain how they differ on portfolio structure, costs, taxation and suitability
